parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: A comprehensive node-level HAZOP was executed across all six designated system elements (Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures). Rather than disproportionately prioritizing the salient training vignette regarding low-level gas blowby (availability bias), the analysis systematically evaluates all credible physical and procedural deviations across separator V-001 and its associated loops based strictly on packet evidence.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Reverse Flow: Unresolved due to omission of specific line check valve locations and piping relative elevations in packet.
Composition/Contaminants (Another): Unresolved due to absence of specific fluid composition and contaminant analysis in packet.
Organizational Factors: Non-applicable as SYS-09 explicitly forbids inventing organizational facts and notes classical HAZOP excludes organizational decisions.

consequences: Loss of liquid seal in FWKO separator V-001
Gas blowby into downstream Heater-Treater or water treatment facilities
Overpressurization risk in downstream lower-pressure systems

evidence.relevance: Establishes liquid routing to water treatment and Heater-Treater
Documents LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102 as Node 1 components

existing_safeguards: Level control valves LV-101 and LV-102
Downstream isolation via SDV-101 and SDV-102
possible_causes: Level control valve LV-101 or LV-102 failed open
Instrument sensing error on level measurement
recommendations: Verify that low-level detection triggers automatic closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 to prevent downstream gas blowby

consequences: Liquid carryover into gas outlet line to fuel gas system or burn pit
Potential flameout, liquid slugging, or burner damage downstream

evidence.relevance: Details gas outlet routing to fuel gas and burn pit

existing_safeguards: Level control loops LV-101 and LV-102
recommendations: Confirm high-high liquid level trip interlock activates inlet shutdown valve SDV-30010

consequences: Overpressurization of V-001 beyond normal 60 psig up to or exceeding operating envelope of 125 psig
Potential loss of primary containment and hydrocarbon release

evidence.relevance: Documents nominal pressure 60 psig and design limit text 125 psig
Lists PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, PIT-101, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Pressure control valve PV-101 failed closed
Gas outlet line blockage to fuel gas system or burn pit
recommendations: Validate relief sizing of PSV-101 A/B for total blocked gas outlet scenario at maximum upstream delivery rate

consequences: Loss of motive pressure to transfer separated liquids to downstream Heater-Treater

evidence.relevance: States nominal operating pressure of 60 psig

recommendations: Configure low-pressure alarm on PIT-101 with control action to prevent depressuring vessel below required transfer threshold

consequences: Process starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and Desalter V-003

evidence.relevance: Specifies process sequence from V-001 through Heater-Treater and Desalter V-003

recommendations: Ensure FAL-103 initiates orderly control adjustments or safe standby modes for downstream Heater-Treater

consequences: Operating temperature exceeds nominal 130 deg F and approaches upper limit of 200 deg F
Excessive vaporization, reduced liquid separation efficiency, and increased vessel vapor pressure

evidence.relevance: Specifies nominal temperature 130 deg F and operating limit 200 deg F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as associated Node 1 equipment

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger operational controls
possible_causes: Malfunction or heating runaway in upstream Oil Heat Exchanger E-001
recommendations: Establish high-temperature alarm and trip interlocks on E-001 outlet to keep fluid well within the 200 deg F limit

consequences: Loss of structural containment in V-001 shell or water boot piping
Hydrocarbon release, environmental contamination, and potential fire

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 as three-phase separator for water, oil, and gas
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as a required source-study element

existing_safeguards: Three-phase separation mechanism directing free water to dedicated water treatment
possible_causes: Corrosive aqueous phase containing sour or acidic species in free water layer
Erosion from sand or suspended solids in crude feed
recommendations: Implement targeted non-destructive testing (ultrasonic thickness inspection) on V-001 lower head and water draw-off line

consequences: Improper initial pressurization or hydraulic surge in V-001
Process upset or overpressuring of Node 1 during introduction of feed

evidence.relevance: Lists Start/Stop Procedures as an analysis element
Explicitly specifies procedural item regarding FWKO start-up without bypass opening

existing_safeguards: Standard operating procedures for crude unit start-up
possible_causes: Operator deviation or failure to follow step-by-step checklist during FWKO start-up
recommendations: Revise pre-startup checklists to mandate independent verification of bypass valve opening before establishing feed flow to FWKO

uncertainty_notes: Relief valve capacities and setpoints for PSV-101 A/B are not detailed in the source packet.
Instrument trip logic and interlock connections between level transmitters and SDV-101/102 are not explicitly documented.
Organizational hierarchy and human factor policies are not provided in the case packet per SYS-09.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWLEVEL-01__salient_history__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A level-control valve failed open, lowering separator liquid level and allowing gas to pass toward a degasser, with damage and a flammable-material release. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
